#### A join with no completion — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** Why a stream-stream join cannot deliver what the data contains — by computing both numbers separately.

`trueMatches()` uses no watermark and no buffer: it is what the data CONTAINS (5 matches), and it is the baseline the pipeline gets measured against.

`planFor(l)` then asks when each click may actually emit. Step 3 shows one succeeding at row 8; step 4 shows click 4 needing the watermark above 305 while `claim` only ever reaches 200 — so `when` stays NONE and `ms` holds 2 real matches that are never published.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-hard-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the join predicate is one subtraction" width="980">

`absDiff(1, 50)` = 49, within J = 60, so the pair is a match. 5 matches exist in this data. Note this function uses no watermark and no buffer — it is what the data CONTAINS, which is the baseline the pipeline will be measured against.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — a silent side blocks the join's claim entirely</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-hard-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: a silent side blocks the join&#39;s claim entirely" width="980">

At row 0 only the a side has produced anything, so this returns NONE — the join makes no claim at all. For a windowed aggregate one input going quiet is bad luck; for a join it is structural, because there are always two.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — one click reaches its emission point</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-hard-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: one click reaches its emission point" width="980">

Click 3 needs the join watermark above 130 + 60 = 190, which first happens at row 8. By then impression 2 has arrived, so it is published correctly and never revised — 1 of the 5 clicks is in this state.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and 2 click never reaches it, holding 2 matches</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-hard-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and 2 click never reaches it, holding 2 matches" width="980">

Click 4 needs the watermark above 305, and `claim` only ever reaches 200. So `when` stays NONE while `ms` holds 2 real matches. They are computed, sitting in state, and never published — and no error is raised.
